title: One hue outside the circle
question: Does the grey read as land that has been STOPPED - or as a game that has not finished loading?
context_md:
Treatment **C**, on a key (`L`) beside **E**, which stays the default. Same world, same seed, same frame - the only difference is how held ground is drawn.

Outside the circle the hue is replaced and **the luminance is kept exactly**, which is why every silhouette, shadow and stratum still reads. It is a full replace on a ramp rather than a blend, for the reason `CLAUDE.md` records: a magnitude-scaled blend once produced a sheet that read as blank.

The colour you can see is the gnome's **carried quickening** - the small free circle that follows him. There is still no drawn rim; that patch of green and brown IS the boundary, which is the first time it has been visible at all.

**Something I did not plan, and it is your call.** The sky stays blue in both - sky is not drawn through the per-cell path, so the transform never touches it. A blue sky over a grey land might be exactly right, or it might be the thing that breaks it.

**Please ignore:** the gnome is standing where the terrain put him, there is no HUD, and E is still the default so nothing changes unless you press `L`.
